lines: For two years I took the 7:40 ferry across the bay, and for two years I told no one on it anything true.
A man in a green raincoat held the door whenever I was late, which was often.
The winter my sister was sick I stopped sleeping, and one morning I simply sat down on the wet deck steps and did not go inside.
The man in the green raincoat sat down beside me.
He took a flask from his pocket, poured something hot into its lid, and handed it over, and we watched the city come toward us through the fog like a slow, lit-up animal.
Years later I saw him on a platform and he lifted two fingers, the way you greet a person who has been inside your worst morning with you.
The ferry knew everything about us.
That is the secret of a good boat.
It holds you for forty minutes and asks for nothing but that you arrive.
